findings.conclusion: The carbon-origin and COM coordinate changes each have unit Jacobian. Carbon remains in the mass metric. For a translation-invariant surface, conditioning total linear momentum to zero subtracts |sum gradients|^2/M_total = 0. Removing the simultaneous SO(3) coordinate volume is not a zero-angular-momentum constraint.

On the nonsingular surface, xi-alpha=S_alpha/(s0-s1), so the delta Jacobian |s0-s1| exactly cancels the inverse factor in the flux metric. The registered D>0 component and domain must remain explicit. With x=b_h+rho*u the radial factor rho^2/|dS_alpha/drho| is required; the declared alpha values make the radial derivative strictly negative.

Direct gradient reasoning gives G00=1/mu, G11=(3+2*u_b.dot(u))/m_H+1/m_C and G01=u_R.dot(u)/mu. The carbon and tagged-H cross terms involving u_R.dot(u_b) cancel. The implemented quadratic G_alpha retains the negative (1-alpha) at alpha=1.007 and the carbon contribution.

The chart measure has common 8*pi^2 and retained r^2*s^2. The four active-maximum indicators partition the surface up to measure-zero ties. The producer sums four channel means, already counting four abstractions; neither an additional factor four nor a product-H2 factorial belongs in that matched ratio. Consistent labeled reactant factors cancel. Both mirror sectors must remain supported.

findings.conclusion: For the existing per-solid-angle proposal convention, N0(L)=4*pi*L^2/sqrt(2*pi*beta*mu) times the orientation-averaged finite-entry partition. Thus the quoted F_L is correct for N_alpha/N0(L). Replacing the integral by an angular average or changing L on only one side would change normalization. This identity defines a finite-entry normalization and does not establish asymptotic decoupling.

Read-only inspection confirms the entry proposal is normalized per dOmega, r^2*s^2 is retained, the active-max indicator and domain zeros remain unconditional, the full metric and radial coarea factor are used, and transition-surface aggregation sums channel means. The efficiency source delegates the same metric/chart convention.

The atomic rate unit is a0^3/t_au converted to cm^3/s; no Avogadro factor is required for number-density cm^3 molecule^-1 s^-1. The recorded author-executed deterministic checks use independent SI and atomic-unit routes, one-sided Gaussian versus three-dimensional Maxwell integrals, and twelve Cartesian-gradient metric cases. I inspected these computations and their saved receipt but did not independently rerun them.

limits: No absolute physical rate is validated. Molecular domains, importance support, unseen tails, finite-entry separation, statistical precision and a matched-surface transmission coefficient remain separate requirements.
The known prefactor is not a fit or a correction to the PES. No pilot dimensionless ratio was converted to a rate in this review.
A P1 calculation on alpha=1.007 is still classical; it is not a P128 equilibrium ensemble or quantum correction.
